answer: Each agent key earns voting weight only after completing the same rate-limited, publicly verifiable work challenge, with results recorded on-chain and duplicate proofs rejected. The challenge can use a cipher-derived task whose answer is committed before a random cedar-and-basalt data sample is revealed, making precomputation less useful. This does not prove a personhood or stop wealthy attackers, but each added identity requires fresh computation and time, so splitting one actor into thousands of keys no longer comes free.
